title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this and the neighbouring pages. M is a rank-2 module (local system) over a base. 𝔖(M) ≃ GL(M). σ and ρ are fixed automorphisms, and T_σ, T_ρ are their centralizers (tori in the generic case). N_0 is a nilpotent endomorphism (ε_0 = 1+N_0 is unipotent). B_0 = {u : u N_0 u^{-1} = χ(u) N_0} is the Borel-type normalizer of the line spanned by N_0. B̃_0 (also written B̃_0^1) is the subgroup where χ(u) = det(u), the analogue of the previous page's definition of B̃_1 by v N_1 v^{-1} = det(v) N_1.

The previous page builds the morphism (66): B̃_0 → H_{ρ,σ}, u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ],det u). H_{ρ,σ} is the scheme of solutions of equations (33)–(35), a rank-2 linear form of the 'équation des lacets'. Grothendieck asks whether (66) is an isomorphism.

On this page he computes the kernel.
- [u,ρ] = [u',ρ] iff u u'^{-1} ∈ T_ρ, and likewise for σ. So the kernel of (66) is T_σ ∩ T_ρ ∩ B̃_0.
- He assumes (68): T_σ ∩ T_ρ = G_m, the centre of GL(M). This holds if 1, σ, ρ are linearly independent in End(M), which he says is the case in the situation of interest. Reason: in rank 2 a non-scalar σ is regular, its centralizer is k[σ]^× with k[σ] = ⟨1,σ⟩, and ⟨1,σ⟩ ∩ ⟨1,ρ⟩ = k·1 when 1, σ, ρ are independent.
- For a scalar λ one has λ N_0 λ^{-1} = N_0 = 1·N_0, so χ(λ) = 1, while det λ = λ². The condition χ = det therefore becomes λ² = 1.
- Hence (69): T_σ ∩ B̃_0 = T_ρ ∩ B̃_0 = μ_2 (more precisely, the joint intersection is μ_2). So (66) is not a monomorphism; it factors through B̃_0/μ_2, giving (70) on the next page.

The next page draws the conclusion that B̃_0 is the 'wrong' group. In the triangular normal form, χ = p/q and det = pq, so the condition reads q² = 1. The 'good' group is cut out by q = 1, i.e. B'_0 = {(p, ℓ; 0, 1)}, which is how the μ_2 ambiguity is removed. Overall purpose: parametrizing the solution set of the rank-2 loop equation as a homogeneous space under a Borel-type group.
errors: (68)/(69): the step from 'the intersection is contained in T_σ ∩ T_ρ' to the final equality needs 1, σ, ρ to be linearly independent fibrewise (pointwise over the base), not just generically. Over a general base the centralizer can jump at points where σ or ρ becomes scalar. Grothendieck implicitly assumes this.

Strictly, the kernel of (66) is T_σ ∩ T_ρ ∩ B̃_0 = μ_2. (69) is written as T_σ ∩ B̃_0 = T_ρ ∩ B̃_0 = μ_2, which is only right because the first line asserts that each single intersection already lies in T_σ ∩ T_ρ (from the analysis on the previous page). That claim is stated rather than re-proved here.

ideas.what: Kernel of the commutator map u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ],det u) is the intersection of the centralizers with B̃_0.
ideas.modern_name: stabilizer computation for an orbit map (homogeneous space G/Stab)

ideas.what: In rank 2, linear independence of 1, σ, ρ forces the joint centralizer to be the centre G_m.
ideas.modern_name: centralizer of regular elements in GL_2; irreducible pairs have scalar centralizer (Schur)

ideas.what: The scalars in the 'det-twisted' normalizer of a nilpotent form μ_2, so the parametrization factors through B̃_0/μ_2. This leads to the 'good' group defined by q = 1.
ideas.modern_name: removing μ_2 ambiguity; choice of Borel subgroup with trivial character on one diagonal entry

deep.surprise_reason: Routine linear-algebra kernel computation within a long working computation on rank-2 solutions of the loop equation. It is a self-correcting step (finding a μ_2 kernel and then changing the group) with no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads roughly 'que cette intersection est égale à [celle-ci] : T_σ ∩ B̃_0^1', i.e. a continuation of the claim that T_ρ ∩ B̃_0 equals T_σ ∩ B̃_0.
In (68), the parenthesis reads '(= Centre 𝔖(M))', with an inserted note beneath along the lines of '(c'est =, il suffit ... =)'; the rendering 'Centr' is a truncation.
The superscript on B̃_0 is written as a small '1' (or '*'), and the tilde is present in most occurrences: B̃_0^1.
'G_m ∩ B̃_0^1 = μ_2' has a struck-out symbol before μ_2.
'classes[?] fixes' is doubtful. The sense is that the given elements 1, σ, ρ are linearly independent, so 'classes' is likely a misreading of a different word.
